images.caption: Nooks: If You Lived Here You'd Be Home by Now, 2007 at Bumbershoot, a music and arts festival held every Labor Day weekend at Seattle Center, Seattle, Washington, USA. images.filename: The Town Crier, v.12, no.50, Dec. 15, 1917 - DPLA - 7f8bfdc5c12489340a8febb6cb73c86b (page 34).jpg
images.caption:
Annual Christmas Number. Page 17 features advertisement for Carolina Court Apartments on Eastlake Ave. Page 23 article "The New Chief" discusses new Seattle Chief of Police, Joel Warren. Page 26 article "Seattle's First Taste of Warfare" discusses the Battle of Seattle in 1856. Page 27 article "Work in Hand to Be Done" discusses Seattle War Efforts. Page 32 includes photographs of Horace C. Henry's private art gallery. Page 33 article ""Some Seattle Artists and Their Work"" features artwork by local artists such as Edward Forkner, F.J. Crooks, Herbert Webb, Roy Partridge, Spiro Orfans, E. Frere Champney, Sara Visonhaler, F. Tadama, Imogen Cunningham Partridge, Irene Ewing, Gertrude Little, Kathleen Houlahan, Clare Shepard, Hamilton Wolf and Yasushi Tanaka. Page 79 features photograph of soldiers marching on 2nd Ave.


Montage of photos of the Horace and Susan Henry home at 1117 Harvard Avenue North in the Harvard-Belmont District on Seattle's Capitol Hill, and the art gallery they started there, the precursor to the Henry Art Gallery at the University of Washington.
